summary.summary: Covering report presenting the draft Annual Governance Statement for 2025/26 (the AGS itself is Appendix 1, a separate document). Two points matter for a lender. First, the draft AGS has been published alongside the council's draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, with the final versions due by the 31 January 2027 statutory deadline after a further update in October 2026 — the reporting cycle is on its statutory track. Second, the council says no NEW significant governance issues have arisen since the final 2024/25 AGS was approved in February 2026, but the existing ones continue: the draft focuses on updating progress on financial sustainability, improvement and transformation, governance and internal control, leadership capacity, children's services improvement and partnership working. In short, a council still working through a known list of significant issues, with no fresh deterioration disclosed and no figures in this paper.

signals.headline: Draft AGS 2025/26 published alongside the draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, in line with statutory requirements; final accountability statements due by the 31 January 2027 backstop after an October 2026 committee update
signals.why: The unaudited 2025/26 balance sheet is now public and the governance disclosures around it are on the statutory timetable rather than slipping.

compliance.notes: High-quality, Arlingclose-advised strategy: strongest areas are the liability benchmark (charted to the end of the debt profile with all balances and assumptions), the full prudential-indicator suite, the capital strategy/MRP and a comprehensive investment strategy covering the council's ~£60m of service/commercial investments. Weakest areas are formal governance artefacts not restated in the annual documents (no explicit adoption of the TM Code's four clauses; no audit-qualification flag; no explicit sterling-only borrowing statement or paras 51-53 compliance statement; no formal IMPs), and, for a commercial investor, no quantified commercial/service-income dependence ratio. Note: the packet's capital_strategy.url (s134122) was a 2027/28 MTFS-assumptions Cabinet paper with no capital-strategy content; the real Capital/Investment strategies and prudential indicators were read from the MTFS 2026-2030 full report (Annexes 5, 6, B, C). The packet TMSS url (s131504) was a cover report; the real TMSS is Annex 7 (s131505).

news_drafts.headline: Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington accounts for 2025/26 await decision on accounting basis after combined authority set up
news_drafts.lead:
The company that runs economic development for Cheshire and Warrington has not yet settled how its 2025/26 accounts will be prepared, because its future depends on the new Cheshire and Warrington Combined Authority. The question was set out in a financial update to the Cheshire and Warrington Joint Committee, which met on 20 October 2026.

A combined authority is a body run by several councils together, often with a mayor, for transport and economic growth. Once it was established, some or all of the existing activities of Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington (ECW) may be transferred to it or stop altogether. The accounts must be prepared on one of two bases: "going concern", which assumes the company carries on, or "break-up", which assumes it does not. The paper says the accounting basis and related disclosures "need to reflect the current position regarding the potential transfer or cessation of some or all of the Company's existing activities".

The chief finance officers of the councils involved, each known as a section 151 officer, are reviewing which basis to use. A section 151 officer is the council's chief finance officer, who has a legal duty to warn if the council cannot balance its books. The decision is to be made before the ECW board approves the accounts in November 2026. The paper gives no figures for the accounts.
news_drafts.paper_title: Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Financial Update on Q1 2026-27 and Statement of Accounts 2025

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East forecasts a balanced 2026/27 after £24.995m of government-approved support; £15m gap set for 2027/28
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council expects to end 2026/27 with spending matching its budget, but only after applying £24.995m of exceptional financial support (EFS), permission from government to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. The first-quarter budget forecast, before the Corporate Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 19 October, says this matches the amount assumed when the budget was set. Service budgets are forecast to underspend by £1.594m, offset by an equal overspend on central budgets.

The forecast also relies on £5.799m held back for transformation work and £15.358m of general contingency, of which £10.336m is for service pressures and £5.022m for central pressures. The council's chief finance officer says the balanced position also depends on delivering savings, containing demand-led spending, achieving capital receipts (money from asset sales) and managing higher financing costs. The 2026/27 budget included a reset of transformation savings.

The council's improvement and transformation delivery plan was rated Green on three of its four priorities at the end of June 2026. Financial sustainability was rated Amber, "at risk", because of the continued reliance on EFS. For 2027/28 the chief finance officer says "robust and deliverable proposals" are needed to close a £15m funding gap, with the aim of ending that reliance. A separate paper on the 2027/28 budget says stronger financial control and clearer recovery arrangements are now in place, but describes the position as "exceptionally fragile" and usable reserves as "materially below the risk-assessed level".
news_drafts.paper_title: Annex 4 for 2026/27 Budget – Quarter 1 Forecast Outturn

news_drafts.headline: Cheshire East audit committee asks for quarterly reports on delivery against ministerial expectations
news_drafts.lead:
Cheshire East Council's Audit and Governance Committee has asked for quarterly assurance reports on how the council is delivering against ministerial expectations. The request is recorded in the committee's action log for its October 2026 meeting, and the reports are to start from the next appropriate meeting.

The log says the reports should focus on "material exceptions, changes in risk, delivery against ministerial expectations and evidence that improvement is embedded and sustained." It also asks for evidence of organisational and cultural change, including staff survey results and measures of whether improvement has been sustained.

The action log does not set out what the ministerial expectations are, and gives no dates beyond the start of the quarterly cycle. It also gives no figures against which progress would be measured.
news_drafts.paper_title: Audit and Governance Committee Action Log - October 2026

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Financial Update on Q1 2026-27 and Statement o
findings.headline: Life Science Fund 2 portfolio valuation decreased by £104,510 due to one company holding materially revalued downward
findings.detail: The Life Science Fund 2 (total fund balance £3.250m) recorded a valuation decrease of £104,510 in Q1 2026-27, reflecting a significant downward revaluation of one company held in the fund portfolio. This represents approximately 3.2% decline. Life Science Fund 1 valuation (£5.139m) has not yet been updated for 2026-27.
findings.matters: Investment fund performance and individual portfolio company valuations are material to councils' understanding of the return on growth and development investments they oversee
findings.figures: Life Science Fund 2 valuation decrease £104,510; Life Science Fund 2 total balance £3.250m; Life Science Fund 1 balance £5.139m
findings.quote: The Life Science 2 Fund valuation has decreased by £104,510, reflecting a significant reduction in the valuation of one company held in the portfolio.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Financial Update on Q1 2026-27 and Statement o
findings.headline: Marketing Cheshire's Visitor Information Centre forecast to require £19,575 subsidy from Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington
findings.detail: Marketing Cheshire is forecasting a balanced full-year position despite a Q1 deficit of £38,206. However, the Visitor Information Centre (VIC) is forecast to operate at a loss; a subsidy of £19,575 from ECW will be required to deliver a balanced position across both companies. A contingency of c.£0.300m has been created to cover this and other transition costs.
findings.matters: A specific service requiring cross-subsidy indicates underlying commercial or demand weakness; councils with visitor information services will recognise this pattern
findings.figures: Marketing Cheshire Q1 deficit £38,206; VIC subsidy required £19,575
findings.quote: However, the VIC in isolation will require additional contributions of £19,575 from ECW to cover the forecast shortfall in VIC sales and to deliver a net nil balanced position across the two companies.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Financial Update on Q1 2026-27 and Statement o
findings.headline: Chief Executive retirement in early August forecast to increase staffing underspend to c.£0.300m by year end
findings.detail: The Chief Executive retired in early August 2026. Combined with secondments of the Strategy and Public Affairs Director and HR Manager to the Combined Authority, plus reduced hours by the Finance Director and Finance Lead, staffing underspend is forecast to grow from £65,510 at Q1 to approximately £0.300m by year end.
findings.matters: Leadership continuity and vacancy management during major organisational restructuring is material to assessing delivery risk and organisational stability
findings.figures: Q1 staffing underspend £65,510; forecast year-end underspend c.£0.300m
findings.quote: The retirement of the Chief Executive in early August will mean that the staffing underspend will increase and is forecast to rise to approx. £300,000 by year end.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Financial Update on Q1 2026-27 and Statement o
findings.headline: Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington received £5.546m in additional government grant funding not budgeted at 2026-27 approval
findings.detail: The original March 2026 budget has been materially revised upward by unbudgeted government grants: Skills Bootcamp (£4.690m), Careers Hub (£0.190m), and Net Zero (£0.666m). All additional income is matched to additional service delivery expenditure. A revised budget will be presented to the Joint Committee on 20 October 2026 maintaining the original net nil balanced position.
findings.matters: Unanticipated grant arrivals represent both opportunity and baseline-budget impact that finance officers at peer councils will face; understanding how this is being absorbed is relevant to forecasting
findings.figures: Skills Bootcamp £4.690m; Careers Hub £0.190m; Net Zero £0.666m; total net revised variance £5.774m
findings.quote: Skills Bootcamp – extra £4.690m government grant. Careers Hub – extra £0.190m of government and third party funding. Net Zero - £0.666m government grants for Regional Skills Pilot and Community Energy Project.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Financial Update on Q1 2026-27 and Statement o
findings.headline: Enterprise Cheshire and Warrington Q1 deficit of £0.196m driven by timing differences; full year balance forecast
findings.detail: ECW reports a Q1 deficit of £0.196m 但 attributes this entirely to timing mismatches between income receipt and expenditure. Despite this and notwithstanding the early retirement of the Chief Executive in August and major functions transferring to the Combined Authority, the company forecasts a balanced full-year position in line with the approved 2026-27 budget.
findings.matters: Finance directors need to distinguish between timing variance and structural deficit; understanding this company's actual underlying position is material given the concurrent organisational restructuring
findings.figures: Q1 deficit £0.196m; full year forecast balanced position (nil)
findings.quote: The Q1 deficit position is due to timing differences with income not being reflected in the revenue account at the same time as related expenditure has been incurred.
